- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought overreaction.
- When sentiment is flat or negative (≤0.2) and price is consolidating, model often underestimates; add 0.5–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.1–0.3% per day from day 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.6), model misreads momentum; align forecast with sentiment swing midpoint rather than peak.
